title: Qualification and Delivery Standard for Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces
content:
**Standard 1 — Qualification.** A coverage-billed Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces bed qualifies on the class's coverage criteria set and a patient weight between the class's lowest patient weight and highest patient weight; a patient too heavy for the class ordered needs the heavier class.

**Standard 2 — Written order.** A written order older than the class's written-order usability period (the calendar months a written order stays usable to deliver the bed) cannot be delivered.

**Standard 3 — Delivery and assembly.** Delivery follows within the class's business days from a complete order to delivery, on the day of hospital discharge where the class's same-day discharge value is Yes, assembled in the home with the side-rail entrapment check documented where the class's entrapment-check value is Yes.

**Standard 4 — Prior authorization.** When the primary coverage's class requires prior authorization for beds and surfaces, a coverage-billed bed is delivered only once a prior-authorization request on this bed record is approved and the delivery date is within the coverage's prior-authorization validity days of its decision date.

**Standard 5 — Private rental.** A private rental needs only the first month's rent and the delivery fee paid.

**Standard 6 — What is furnished.** The bed furnished is the class's HCPCS code with the class's bed height control and head and foot controls, a sleeping surface of the class's width in inches, and a mattress and side rails where the class includes them in the bed payment; it is assembled in the home by Summit Ridge staff where the class's in-home setup value is Yes.

The class values named above (coverage criteria set, weight range, written-order period, delivery lead, same-day discharge, entrapment check, code, controls, width, mattress, rails and in-home setup) are the bed class's published figures.

## Notes on Standard 4

- The requirement comes from the patient's primary coverage class (whether it requires prior authorization for beds and surfaces) and the validity period comes from that coverage (its prior-authorization validity days); both belong to the Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility records, not to the bed class.
- The approved request must be a prior-authorization request on this bed record. Approval recorded on a different record does not satisfy the standard.
- The evidence is the system record: the request's type, its status, its decision date and the bed record it is attached to, read before delivery.

| Primary coverage class requires prior authorization for beds and surfaces | Approved prior-authorization request on this bed record | Delivery date within the validity days of the decision date | Standard 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Met |
| Yes | Yes | No | Not met — the bed is not delivered on coverage |
| Yes | No | — | Not met — the bed is not delivered on coverage |
| No | — | — | Places no condition on delivery |

### Hypothetical illustration of Standard 4

A coverage class (hypothetically) requires prior authorization and allows 120 validity days. A request on this bed record is approved with a decision date in early March. A delivery 45 days after the decision date is within the validity days; a delivery 150 days after the decision date is not, and Standard 4 is not met for that delivery date.

## Notes on Standards 1 and 5

- Standard 1 governs coverage-billed beds. For a private rental, Standard 5 states that only the first month's rent and the delivery fee need to be paid.
- Under Standard 1, a hypothetical patient whose recorded weight is above the highest patient weight of the class ordered needs the heavier class.
